Function: The jig is used to hold the MPHX plate during the gluing and lamina application processes
Potential Failure Mode: Jig printed in two sections offers no way to ensure linearity
Potential Effects of Failure: Uneven glue distribution
Potential Cause of Failure: Connection point not secure and side walls are not going to be truly perpendicular to jig face
Control Method: Visually inspect operation and glue distribution
Recommended Action: Machine the jig out of metal (single piece)

Function: Adheres MPHX plate and lamina
Potential Failure Mode: Short pot life
Potential Effects of Failure: Won't be able to make as large of a batch before cleaning and or diluting
Potential Cause of Failure: Rollers mixing adhesive causing it to set faster
Control Method: We will be doing tests to attempt to dilute the adhesive and revive the pot
Recommended Action: Dilute adhesive using MEK and acetone

Function: A byproduct of production rate
Potential Failure Mode: Too slow of a cycle time, not enough modules produced
Potential Effects of Failure: Smaller batches/inability to meet desired output
Potential Cause of Failure: Too slow of a production speed
Control Method: Tests for cycle time (how long it takes for one jig to be glued)

Function: Holds the MPHX plates in place
Potential Failure Mode: Surface of the front of the MPHX jig is coated in glue and adheres to the lamina during curing
Potential Effects of Failure: Inability to produce modules (wasted materials), need to reprint and assemble the jigs, significant time and money loss
Potential Cause of Failure: Inaccurate glue distribution
Control Method: Tetectible once the MPHX plate has glue and is placed onto the lamina jig
Recommended Action: Lower the height of the plate slot edge in the 3d print/CAD

Function: Holds the lamina for lamina and plate adhesion
Potential Failure Mode: Ridges on lamina jig prevent jigs from properly applying pressure and adhering the MPHX modules to the lamina
Potential Effects of Failure: The lamina is not in contact with the glued MPHX plate and the two are not bonded/uneven bonding pressure
Potential Cause of Failure: The lamina ridges are too high/extrude to far from the base of the lamina jig causing a space between the lamina and MPHX jigs
Control Method: Tetectible once the MPHX plate has glue and is placed onto the lamina jig
Recommended Action: Decrease the lenghts on the shim stock side rails on the MPHX jig and create mirror indents on the MPHX jig mathching the ridges on the lamina jig

Function: Adhesion
Potential Failure Mode: Insufficient glue application
Potential Effects of Failure: MPHX Plate fails to seal
Potential Cause of Failure: Side ridges are uneven making seal impossible
Control Method: Requires full wet run with pressure test

Function: Holds the MPHX plates and lamina
Potential Failure Mode: Excess glue is applied to jig in unexpected location and adheres the jigs together
Potential Effects of Failure: Inability to seperate jigs and access finished plates. Requiring new jig and wasting module materials
Potential Cause of Failure: Jig features in line with adhesive roller path
Control Method: Adhesive visible on jig surface. Resistance to jig seperation
Recommended Action: Ensure the rollers are always in line with the MPHX jig and ONLY the MPHX jig. Visually inspect side rails prior to lamina application

Function: Holds the jig as it slides over the roller
Potential Failure Mode: Misalignment with feed on other side
Potential Effects of Failure: Jig gets blocked by feed
Potential Cause of Failure: Difficulty in aligning separate 80x20 pieces across large distance
Control Method: Easily detected through basic testing
Recommended Action: Update design to include large cross bars to prevent misalignment

Function: Guide jig over adhesive rollers
Potential Failure Mode: Lack of bearing for guidance to the jig sides
Potential Effects of Failure: Jig catches (feed plate) or essesive friction
Potential Cause of Failure: Side friction on jigs
Control Method: Vissually observation of device in testing
Recommended Action: Add side bearings to desgin of feed plate

Function: Foundational structure holding everything together and inline
Potential Failure Mode: Location of fasteners create bending moment to cause structure to deflect into a U shape
Potential Effects of Failure: Feed is slightly angled and unstable. Can be mitigated by adjusting Feed angle
Potential Cause of Failure: Separate beam on either side means that there is no stabilizing force, allowing it to bend in this fashion
Control Method: Easily detected by rocking frame and checking for feet offset
Recommended Action: Update design to include large cross bars to prevent bending across center plate

Function: Housing for springs that provide pressure to the MPHX plates when adhesive is being applied
Potential Failure Mode: Too much/too little pressure
Potential Effects of Failure: Weak glue joints (poor glue distribution i.e. glue flowing into channels or not enough glue applied)
Potential Cause of Failure: Too much/too little spring compression in top roller housing
Control Method: Do test sample to determine glue distribution
Recommended Action: Increase or reduce number of spacers pushing down on the springs

Function: Adhesion
Potential Failure Mode: Cure time takes longer than expected
Potential Effects of Failure: The longer cure time leads to more time between
Potential Cause of Failure: Glue less chemically compatible with plate due to materials changes
Control Method: Requires a full wet run with subsequent testing

Function: Shim Stock/super glue
Potential Failure Mode: The glue connecting the shim stock to the MPHX jig may be deteriorated due to the fumes from the MEK
Potential Effects of Failure: The shim stock will disconnect from the front of the MPHX plate jig leaving the plate subject to movement and inability to be glued
Potential Cause of Failure: The material/ chemical incompatibiltity
Control Method: Detectible after running the system (visible)
Recommended Action: Use a different adhesive to connect the shim stock

Function: Hold the shim stock on either side of the MPHX and Lamina Jigs
Potential Failure Mode: Jig catching in feed
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to realign jig in feed and possibly start new batch of modules
Potential Cause of Failure: Screw heads catching on edges of feed rails
Control Method: Swap button head screws with flat head screws or modify the feed rails so they are continuous and do not have an edge for the jig to catch on
Recommended Action: Swap button head screws for flat heads

Function: The jigs are used to hold the assembled and unassembled modules during the application systems
Potential Failure Mode: The 3D printed jigs may deteriorate due to the fumes and/or contact with/from the adhesive over time
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to reprint/clean jigs, significant time loss
Potential Cause of Failure: Overapplication/inaccuracy of glue application
Control Method: Visual analysis
Recommended Action: Check the material properties of the current (as well as other 3d printable) filaments and their compatibility with the glue selected

Function: The jigs are used to hold the assembled and unassembled modules during the application systems
Potential Failure Mode: The dovetail pattern connecting the two jigs may not be a secure way to hold the two halves of each jig together due to external forces on the connections
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to reprint/redesign jigs, significant time loss
Potential Cause of Failure: Inability to hold MPHX plate while gluing/ while under pressure
Control Method: Visual/physical analysis
Recommended Action: Reinforce the jigs so that they have shim stock along any parts that are connected

Function: Provides mechanical power to rotate adhesive-application roller bar
Potential Failure Mode: Motor burnout
Potential Effects of Failure: Roller no longer turns --> no more glue application possible + motor replacement needed
Potential Cause of Failure: Mechanical resistance due to adhesive thickening exceeds motor capacity
Control Method: We will be doing tests to determine adhesive thickening rates and how to prevent it; it will be obvious when the bar is no longer spinning when the power is on
Recommended Action: Prevent adhesive from thickening by adding solvent to the pot

Function: Convert power from electrical socket to usable power for the speed controller
Potential Failure Mode: Sparks from wire connection points
Potential Effects of Failure: Sparks or damage to other electrical components that can lead to arcs or short circuits
Potential Cause of Failure: Power surges through the system or improperly secured wire connections between the speed controller and AC/DC power converter
Control Method:
Make sure all wires connecting components are secure and undamaged
Use surge protectors on the associated outlet to prevent power surges from going through the system
Recommended Action: Testing: test to make sure wire connection points are secure

Function: Adhesion
Potential Failure Mode: Insufficient glue application
Potential Effects of Failure: Each plate requires multiple passes, significantly increasing time per plate and decreasing plates per vat.
Potential Cause of Failure: Insufficient traction of roller or poor viscosity of glue
Control Method: May be difficult to detect until samples are glued; viscosity based mitigations easy but roller design mitigations difficult

Function: Housing for springs that provide pressure to the MPHX plates when adhesive is being applied
Potential Failure Mode: Solvent wear
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to 3D print new housing
Potential Cause of Failure: Solvent degrading the PETG
Control Method: Potential way to limit exposure is apply a coating to the plastic to prevent the solvent fumes from penetrating the housing. No matter what there will be exposure.
Recommended Action: Potential way to limit exposure is apply a coating to the plastic to prevent the solvent fumes from penetrating the housing. No matter what there will be exposure.

Function: Holds the lamina for lamina and plate adhesion
Potential Failure Mode: The alignment ridges on the lamina jig do not hold the lamina/allow slippage do to excessive usage
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to reprint or redesign the jig
Potential Cause of Failure: Incorrect lamina and MPHX alignment
Control Method: Visual analysis/physical testing
Recommended Action: Edit the jig CAD's to either allow the ridges to sit within the MPHX jig or shorten the length of the shim stock to prevent interference

Function: The jig is used to hold the MPHX plate during the gluing and lamina application processes
Potential Failure Mode: The 3d printed jig flexes/bows during the lamina application/curing process
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to reprint MPHX jigs
Potential Cause of Failure: Overuse/material decay over time
Control Method: Visually checking the MPHX jigs after stacking
Recommended Action: Test to see how many usages a jig can go through before deformation occurs

Function: Create a path for electricity to travel between components
Potential Failure Mode: Improper securing of wire connection points
Potential Effects of Failure: Inconsistent/ no power moving through the system --> motor doesn't receive enough power to turn the roller
Potential Cause of Failure: Improper assembly of electrical components
Control Method: Manipulate wire connection points to ensure secure connection

Function: Bearing to make axle spin
Potential Failure Mode: Wear
Potential Effects of Failure: Possible need to remanufacture
Potential Cause of Failure: Frictional wear
Control Method: Visual inspection of wear
Recommended Action: Lubricate (can see with a eyes if there is wear)

Function: To move the jig plates through the glue applicator
Potential Failure Mode: Misalignment of bearings locations vertically
Potential Effects of Failure: Uneven support for jig, offset approach angle for jig into roller
Potential Cause of Failure: Incorrect assembly, poor adjusting, not meeting tolerances
Control Method: Somewhat easily detected by measuring angles and checking alignment
Recommended Action: Tighten tolerances for bearing placement, create better procedure to ensure that feed plates are properly leveled.

Function: Connects to the AC/DC converter and allows power from outlet to power the motor
Potential Failure Mode: Fuse Blows
Potential Effects of Failure: Need to replace fuse
Potential Cause of Failure: To much current
Control Method: Test circuit beforehand

Function: Applies glue to plate, and uses friction to pull the plate along
Potential Failure Mode: Plate is not pulled through properly, causing jig to stop/stutter
Potential Effects of Failure: Uneven/over application of glue
Potential Cause of Failure: Knurling on rollers becomes worn down/kurling is not deep enough. Alternatively, glue within the knurling cures, reducing the depth of the groves
Control Method: It will be visually obvious that the jig is no longer moving
Recommended Action: First, increase the top roller pressure to increase the friction force clean rollers. If cleaning the rollers does not fix this, the roller may need to re-machined

Function: Bearings provide contact surface for jig before and after it passes through the roller.
Potential Failure Mode: Support Bars, fastened using friction nuts, can become loose
Potential Effects of Failure: Bars loose set vertical alignment with the roller, causing the jig to enter/leave the roller at an angle
Potential Cause of Failure: Repeated impacts or vibration to support bars
Control Method: By marking the set distances, visual inspection can reveal when the support bars have moved. Additionally, properly torquing and using lock tight can ensure the screw does not become loose

Function: Hold 2 or more parts together
Potential Failure Mode: Chemical corrosion
Potential Effects of Failure: System adjustment becomes difficult adjust
Potential Cause of Failure: Exposure to glueing adhesive
Control Method: Can be found through visual inspection

Function: Create a level surface on which to operate the device and prevent system from moving on the workspace
Potential Failure Mode: Wear over time/ possible breakage of rubber component
Potential Effects of Failure: Non-level system support and increased probability for manufacturing errors
Potential Cause of Failure: Movement of system by operator during assembly/ operation can put pressure on the sides of the rubber attachments
Control Method: It will be obvious if traction points are damaged and in need of replacement
